tldr: On a stipulated two-contrast Gaussian experiment, the sharp recruitment frontier protects the subgroup with the largest realized loss under actual fractional deployment. Certified finite programs determine \(C_{\max}(\alpha,v)\), all optimal limiting shares and total original-record fraction rules. Positive priorities yield a strict fractional joint-information advantage; the balanced fractional constant satisfies \(101/500<C_{\max}<211/1000\). Hu et al. use binary subgroup policies and a maximum after expectation. For the realized maximum on the same Gaussian benchmark, randomized binary policies inherit the fractional lower bound, while a total coordinate sign rule supplies an upper bound and proves \(V_N^{\rm bin}=\Theta(N^{-1/2})\). At balanced parameters and \(4\mid N\), \(101/500<\sqrt N V_N^{\rm bin}\le\kappa\sqrt2<121/500\). The sharp binary constant and its optimal design remain undetermined.
